newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher but still cautious.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher but still cautious.

text.p: A large flow of buying orders towards the end of the session pushed Argentine stocks higher Friday.
Still, trade remained cautious and thin in anticipation of the U.S. presidential election on Tuesday.
The blue-chip Merval .MERV index rose 0.60 percent to 573.90, while the general stock index gained 0.20 percent.
"The market continued to demonstrate large selectivity," said Jose Napoli, a trader at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
This has produced a "climate of slim interest in certain sectors, like oil. The market is very expectant and there is a lack of liquidity," added Napoli.
The market was waiting for the release of U.S. employment figures, which turned out as the market had expected, lending support to stocks.
Trade volume fell to $10.5 million from $12.5 million on Thursday.
Of the 63 stocks traded this session, 17 rose, 18 fell and 28 were unchanged.
Among the main listed firms, steel maker Acindar and construction firm Polledo posted the largest gains. Acindar rose 5.15 percent and Polledo rose 4.21 percent.

Traders said next week's activity is likely to be largely decided by the outcome of the U.S. vote. The election results will have an impact on U.S. Treasuries, which in turn will affect Argentine stocks.
Market players said the performance of the Mexican peso will also be closely watched next week by Argentine stock traders.
In addition, traders are anticipating the release of quarterly results for the larger Argentine companies including oil giant YPF.
